title: POC weekly sync - model selection & pinning (Orion Retail)
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark spreadsheet with per-route latency and cost (Sanjay)
Customer to run the model-pinned smoke tests on staging and report errors (Alex)
Schedule a rollback drill with SE-run playbook next Tuesday (Morgan)
Send SOC2 + network diagram to Tom (Jules)
action_items: Sanjay: share benchmark CSV and pinned model configs by EOD 2027-09-01
Alex: run 1000 sample inference requests through pinned route and upload logs by 2027-09-03
Morgan: prepare rollback runbook and fallback policy doc by 2027-09-02
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latest benchmark results across candidate models, confirm a pinned model for pilot, and outline rollback/fallback policies. Customer sees slightly higher tail latency on v2 quantized model; team to validate pin to v1 with fallback to v2-small when under capacity strain.
transcript:
Header: 2027-08-31 11:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sanjay (Redwood AE), Morgan (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood CSM), Alex (Orion Eng), Priya (Orion Head of ML), Tom (Orion Platform), Dana (Orion PM)

00:00:03 - Sanjay: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — go over the latest benchmarks, model pinning recommendation, fallback/rollback plan and next steps.
00:00:22 - Alex: Yep, thanks. we ran the overnight suite, so I have the numbers.
00:00:35 - Morgan: great, and I posted the per-route histogram in the sheet, it's under tab "latency-summaries". there are some odd tails on the v2-quant run.
00:00:50 - Priya: when you say "v2-quant" you mean the 8-bit quantized variant from the catalog? sometimes the names get mixed up in the export, just want to be clear.
00:01:03 - Morgan: yes, it's the 8-bit distill variant, catalog id redwood-v2-q8.
00:01:15 - Tom: quick note, our staging cluster has slightly smaller gpus than prod so absolute numbers will be up to 15% worse in staging. we accounted for that in the sheet.
00:01:29 - Jules: good call, thanks.

00:03:05 - Alex: jumping in on results: median latency across the set for redwood-v1-lf was 120ms, p95 310ms, p99 720ms. for redwood-v2-q8 median 95ms, p95 480ms, p99 1.2s — so better median but worse tail.
00:03:28 - Priya: that's the part that worries us, the p99 spikes are what will affect user experience during spikes.
00:03:41 - Morgan: right, we think that's due to KV cache churn combined with longer prefix lengths on some of your routes. the runtime's continuous batching sometimes causes extra stalls with q8 kernels under those sequences.
00:03:58 - Alex: we've got a lot of long-context queries for order-history retrieval. those are the ones hitting the p99.
00:04:12 - Sanjay: ok so operationally we can recommend pinning the pilot to redwood-v1-lf as primary and set redwood-v2-q8 as fallback for cost-controlled bulk runs. that gives consistent tail with slightly higher token cost.
00:04:34 - Dana: cost difference? what's the delta per 1M tokens?
00:04:41 - Morgan: roughly 22% higher token cost on v1-lf vs v2-q8 in our estimates given your observed batch sizes. the sheet has per-route breakdown.
00:04:58 - Alex: do we have a suggestion for batch sizes / concurrency to reduce p99 on v2-q8?
00:05:06 - Morgan: yes, we recommend smaller max_batch_size for order-history route — set to 8 instead of 32, and enforce max_concurrency of 40. that helps avoid big batching stalls. also enable prefix-level KV caching for the repeated customer prompt segments. note: sometimes the export shows "KV cash" — it's KV cache.
00:05:30 - Priya: will that reduce cost? smaller batch means less throughput so maybe cost goes up.
00:05:38 - Morgan: tradeoff, yeah. smaller batch reduces batching latency but increases per-token overhead. net cost change depends on utilization; on your traffic pattern we saw a small +3-5% cost, but p99 drops significantly.

00:08:00 - Tom: on pinning — what's the rollback story if we pin to v1 and then need to revert to v2 or to a different variant?
00:08:12 - Sanjay: we've got a canary + auto-fallback plan. primary route pinned to v1, we keep v2-q8 as an alternate with health checks. if p95/p99 exceeds thresholds for 3 minutes we automatically route 30% of traffic to the alternate, then 0% if errors increase. we also have manual rollback runbook that SE can execute to revert pinning quickly.
00:08:45 - Morgan: and we recommend keeping model version tags in the route config, don't use bare "latest". pin by model_id:version so you get reproducibility.
00:09:00 - Alex: understood. can you send the exact route config snippet? hard for us to translate from the console UI.
00:09:08 - Morgan: yes, I'll paste a YAML snippet in the sheet and the workbook.

00:11:20 - Priya: question on privacy: we need to know if any user-level tokens are stored in the platform logs and how long logs are retained.
00:11:33 - Jules: good question, Tom is our CSM but I can answer: by default logs are redacted, and for Private/Dedicated customers you can configure retention and push to your own S3. we'll attach the SOC2 and network diagram.
00:11:52 - Tom (customer): to be explicit, we'd prefer audit logs forwarded to our Splunk for 90 days. is that supported?
00:11:59 - Jules: yes, we can set up log forwarder; I'll include configuration steps.

00:14:10 - Alex: back to benchmarks — we also ran with int4 experimental quant and saw odd hallucination increases on a small sample, likely due to quant noise on long-context retrieval.
00:14:26 - Morgan: yep int4 is still experimental in the catalog; we recommend not using int4 for the pilot. keep it for cost experiments only.

00:16:00 - Dana: any thoughts about using Dedicated capacity vs Hosted for pilot? we want predictable latency but hosting costs are a concern.
00:16:15 - Sanjay: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better tail characteristics because you control the pool. but it comes with reserved commitment. Hosted with pinning plus autoscale and fallback policies can be fine for pilot — and it's lower up-front.
00:16:33 - Priya: our timeline: pilot needs to be production-like by mid-September. does that push us to Dedicated?
00:16:42 - Morgan: it's borderline — if you expect steady sustained load by mid-September, we can discuss a short reserved capacity window or a Dedicated trial. otherwise host and monitor, and we can flip to Dedicated as an ops exercise if tails persist.

00:19:05 - Alex: logs from the sample run show some retry storms when p99 spikes, do you have recommendations to limit retries?
00:19:15 - Morgan: yes, client-side: exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries to 2. server-side: our runtime will auto-throttle if error rates increase; we also can set circuit-breaker thresholds in the route.
00:19:30 - Dana: ok good.

00:22:10 - Sanjay: quick demo — Morgan, can you show the console route where we pin model and configure fallback?
00:22:22 - Morgan: sure, sharing screen — so here is the route page, under Model Selection choose model_id redwood-v1-lf@v1.2.3, add fallback redwood-v2-q8@v2.0.1 with health-check interval 10s. set traffic shift policy: canary 10% for 5m then 100% if healthy, fallback on error 30% immediate.
00:23:05 - Tom: will that preserve per-route quota? we have quotas per api-key.
00:23:13 - Morgan: yes quotas are per-route per-key and follow the routing — when traffic shifts the quota applies accordingly.

00:25:00 - Alex: any gotchas for model pinning when we update model weights (minor patch)? do we need to change version tags?
00:25:12 - Morgan: yes, any actual weight changes should use a new model version. non-breaking metadata changes can keep the tag but we advise recording the model checksum and changelog in the route annotations.
00:25:28 - Priya: ok.

00:28:40 - Alex: suggested acceptance criteria for pilot: p95 < 400ms and p99 < 900ms on critical routes, <1% error rate, and cost within 15% of our target. does that sound reasonable?
00:28:54 - Sanjay: yes that's actionable — we'll help instrument checks.

00:31:10 - Morgan: next: fallback/rollback drill. propose we run a scheduled rollback test on staging where we intentionally degrade v1 (inject increased latency) and observe auto-fallback triggers and manual rollback steps. SE will run, customer to observe.
00:31:28 - Alex: sounds good, when?
00:31:33 - Morgan: propose 2027-09-07 10am PT.
00:31:38 - Dana: works for us.

00:34:50 - Jules: security docs will be sent after this call — SOC2, ISO, KMS notes and network diagram.
00:35:02 - Tom: thanks. also please include details on SAML/SSO setup for our engineers.
00:35:09 - Jules: will do.

00:38:00 - Sanjay: recap: recommend pin primary to redwood-v1-lf@v1.2.3, set redwood-v2-q8@v2.0.1 as fallback with healthchecks, reduce batch on order-history route to 8, enable prefix KV cache, don't use int4 for pilot. SE to prepare rollback drill on 2027-09-07. Red team to send benchmarks, SOC2 and network diag.
00:38:30 - Alex: agreed.
00:38:40 - Priya: quick clarifying question — for the canary policy thresholds you suggested, can we shorten canary window to 2 minutes for faster rollouts?
00:38:52 - Morgan: yes you can, but smaller windows give less signal. 5m recommended, 2m is ok if you have synthetic checks running.
00:39:15 - Dana: ok we'll try 2m with synthetic checks.

00:41:00 - Sanjay: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheet and the runbook.
00:41:10 - Jules: thanks all.
00:41:20 - Alex: thanks.

End of transcript.
